4. Evidence was adduced by the parties In support of their respective contentions. On behalf of the plaintiffs one witness was examined whereas defendant No. 2 examined himself on behalf of the contesting defendants. D.W. 2 was examined for defendant No. 1 to claim a saham. Certain Khatians were produced by the plaintiffs to prove that their names appear in that record of rights. 

 5. The learned Subordinate Judge on consideration of the materials on record rejected the defence case of benami as set out by them. He also rejected their claim as regards absence of title of the plaintiffs and defendant No. 1 on the basis of inheritance. The learned Subordinate Judge noticed the entries in the record of right and held that the plaintiff and defendant No. 1 were heirs of Akram Ali, and as such their claims were recorded in the khatian of the 1st schedule land which belonged to Akram Ali. He further held that the entry in the record of right was true and correct. As regards 2nd schedule of land the learned Subordinate Judge similarly rejected the defence case and held that the plaintiffs had 1/3rd share therein. The learned Subordinate Judge accordingly hold that the schedule I land belonged to Akram Ali alone and schedule 2 land belonged to Akram Ali and defendant 2 jointly ill terms of the kabuliyat Ext. 2 and in the relevant record of right the entries were according y made correctly. On the aforesaid basis the learned Subordinate Judge held that the plaintiffs have 1/3rd share in the 2nd schedule land and 2/3rd share in the 1st schedule land.
